summary: Yoshihiko Sakurai specializes in Buddhist studies, having studied at Ryukoku University. He served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and as a researcher at the Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Center.
Yoshihiro Hayashi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. In 2009, he was attested as a part-time lecturer at both Ritsumeikan University and Shitennoji University.
Yoshihiro Matsunami is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1991–1999) and became its president in 2001.

Yoshihito Muroji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Hamburg in 1992. He held posts at Kyoto University, Koyasan University, and Shiga University of Medical Science.
Yoshiki Motoaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who was affiliated with Otani University (attested 2013) and the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Yoshimi Nozawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. As of 2026, he is attested as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yoshinobu Kimoto is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities. He served at Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College, as president of Koshien Junior College (2000–2012), and professor at Ryukoku University (2013–2021).
Yoshinobu Sakade was a Sinologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1954–1963) under Mitsuji Fukunaga. He later served on the faculty at Kansai University from around 1975 to 2005.

Yoshinori Takeuchi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (1959–1976) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1976–1988).

Yoshio Kawakatsu was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University and under Paul Demiéville, later serving as a library-track assistant at Kyoto University from around 1948 to 1984.
Yoshio Nishiguchi is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who was educated under the instruction of Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Yoshio Takeuchi was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1907 to 1910 and held a post at Tohoku University from circa 1923 to 1947.

Yoshiro Imaeda is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Otani University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He held positions at the CNRS, the National Library of Bhutan, UC Berkeley, and Kyoto University.

Yoshiro Tamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He held professorships at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo (1972–1982), and Rissho University (~1982–1989).

Yoshitaka Iriya was a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held professorships at Nagoya University, Kyoto University, and Kyoto Sangyo University.
Yoshito S. Hakeda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor and associate professor at Columbia University, remaining there until 1983.
Yoshitoyo Ohara is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held affiliations at Kyoto University (attested 2006) and Kyoto National Museum (attested 2016).

Yoshitsugu Sawai is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities under John B. Carman and others. He served as a professor and dean of human studies at Tenri University (~1984–2017).

Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held several posts at Taisho University (attested 1998–2026) and served as a visiting researcher at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe is a scholar in computational sciences and Tibetology who studied at Tohoku University. He worked at Tohoku University (1975–2012, 2018), held posts at JAIST and NII, and founded the Asian Consortium on Computational Materials Science.
